steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher A
steps.text: How goes it, Kelly?

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher B
steps.text: Just finished logging the Polar Area's plant monitoring data. Most of our fifty-three newcomer plants show no abnormal traits, and have survived the initial observation period. But as you can see here...

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher A
steps.text: This Sheath Zelkova by the door? These two severely curled up leaves are a sign of dehydration.

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher A
steps.text: That patch of Icefield Cottongrass is clearly still growing, but the number of cotton balls hasn't been increasing much, and the amount of cotton fiber is lower than normal too.

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher B
steps.text: That Square Sunflower is our most obvious case. Its disc florets should be always extending towards the sun, but it's drooping so low it's almost touching the soil.

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher A
steps.text: All within expectations. We've only just begun planning out the vivarium's Polar Area, so we're lacking both data for integration and accumulated experience.

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher A
steps.text: Quick, go ask Director Muelsyse about it. She'll definitely know where the problems lie.

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher B
steps.text: (Speaking of which, there's something magical about the way the Director knows plants so well. Everyone's been secretly wondering if she really can talk to plants.)

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher A
steps.text: (Don't go spouting nonsense now.)

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Kelly, try resetting the parameters of this area's circulation system, and add some mycorrhiza bacteria to the substrate to promote the absorption of water and nutrients.

steps.name: Ecological Section Researchers A & B
steps.text: Director Muelsyse!

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher B
steps.text: ...But the parameters were precisely configured according to the data sent by Miss Magallan.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It's true that Maggy sent the plants, but she's just an explorer. What does she know about botany?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Every bit of biological data she collected is only true for when these plants are growing in Sami.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The vivarium is still too 'warm' for them.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Try lowering the temperature and humidity a little.

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher B
steps.text: Alright, Director.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Next up is inspecting the Plateau Zone, right? Let's head there together.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: (Moving fingers contentedly)

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: (Vigorously stretching)

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: Be careful, Sheath Zelkova. Your fingers have been curled up all this time, so take care to not strain your veins when stretching them out so suddenly.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: Hey, don't get me started. Quit moving around so much, your cotton's flying all over my face.

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: What did that guy say earlier? The plateau area is just a little further up? Maybe we can talk to the legendary Stipa if I send my cotton flying a bit further.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: You only just left Sami, so everything feels new to you, huh.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: Hey, Square Sunflower. Why so quiet?

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: He's wilting. Where's his energy gone? I guess he's still not used to the new environment yet.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: No, I haven't seen him eating or drinking at all, so my guess is that he's feeling a little moody.
So they do have emotions.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: Who said that?

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: ...It's raining.

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: It can rain indoors? Or is this that so-called circulation system?

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: What sort of rain is this? Why are the droplets sticking to my branches? I can't shake them off.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hiya, fellas. Let's reacquaint ourselves, shall we? I'm Muelsyse.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: You're here again.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Whoopsie daisy. I went to find Nasti to modify some equipment. She's not exactly the chatty type, so it took some time.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Anyhow, you guys are looking way peppier than before.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: We make do.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: At least you haven't been curling up your leaves on purpose, right?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I'm gonna be personally overseeing the Polar Area until the second batch of plants arrives next month, okay?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: So I'll be switching up your substrate at noon. I redid the new formula according to the soil samples I got from Sami.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You'll get all the yummy nutrients you need through the 'rain' or 'dew' at random. We're scrapping the 'regular' pattern.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Lemme know if you need anything else. Terrain, air, soil, water, climate... what are the optimal conditions for you to survive? Don't be shy now, me and the vivarium don't judge.

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: You're so patient with us, Muelsyse.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I actually included a Polar Area when I first planned this place out, but no one from Ecological had been to Sami back then. So we shelved it.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But I've been directing ecological experiments at Rhine for the past few years, so I thought we had a solid enough foundation to...

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: Why Sami?

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: Many see it as an inaccessible and frigid region. Sealed off, isolated, mysterious, dangerous.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Well, it's not just Sami I'm interested in. I've got my peepers on every special ecosystem in Terra.

spans.text: Sami I'm interested in. I've got my peepers on every special ecosystem in Terra.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Sami's just specialer than most. Wetlands, forests, and icefield, in that order. A weird combo, really... Hmm, how do I put it? A little 'forced'?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Plus, while it is absolutely freezing compared to the centrum, it's got abnormally abundant biodiversity that doesn't conform to the laws of ecology at all.

spans.text: absolutely freezing compared to the centrum, it's got abnormally abundant biodiversity that doesn't conform to the laws of ecology at all.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: So my best guess is that Sami's just really 'clean.'

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: 'Clean'?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I took some physiological samples from you guys... The amount of Originium granules in your root systems is way lower than average.

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: Could you try dumbing that down for a plant?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Sami is by far the best environment for my experiments.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: So, you want to recreate a 'Sami' in this giant glass house?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: A glass house... uh-huh.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: But why, Muelsyse?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Because I'm the youngest and bestest ecologist here at Rhine Lab, of course!

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I've got both the ability and the responsibility to turn this glass house here into the cleanest place in Terra. It'll have the freshest air, the most hospitable climate, and the most nutritious soil.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It'll have the richest ecosystem ever, for every kind of fragile lifeform to freely thrive in.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: That's what I've always been... um, pursuing?

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: (Forcefully shedding cotton)

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: (Shaking branches and leaves freely)

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hehe, thankies.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: Is that something worth applauding?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Square Sunflower! You scared the spit outta me, suddenly opening your mouth like that!

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: He's been like that ever since he arrived, more than half a month ago.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: What a downer. He's always sulking about something.

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: He's still brooding over how he got transplanted from the forests of Sami to a strange city.

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: But what's done is done, so why not just get used to it here? One of my cotton balls floated into the water of the compartment next door, and I could taste the 'seawater's saltiness.'

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: Who knows? If you'd stayed in Sami you might be manure by now. The seeds of your special disc florets make you both fowlbeast fodder and a digestive aid for carnivores with big appetites.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: You should spit out your cotton properly before spouting all that nonsense.

steps.name: Icefield Cottongrass
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: Muelsyse. Don't you want to know why I've been wilting since I got here? Aren't you curious?

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: A Square Sunflower's disc florets will always face the sun. True, your vivarium's lighting system can even simulate how the sunlight changes at different times of day.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: It's very... what you people would call, 'advanced.'

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: ...But in the end, it's no sun.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: The real sun is outside your glass house. But remove this layer of glass, and this mix of soil, air, temperature, moisture, and microbial clusters will no longer be tenable.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: Even if you perfectly replicated each and every grain of soil, gust of cold wind, and block of ice from Sami, this place would still be no different from the specimen box you put me in to bring me here.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Well... compared to most other plants, the way you photosynthesize is kinda special, so there's not much I can do about that.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: That's not what I meant.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: No, I gotcha.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Oceans, mudflats, forests, deserts, the Black Flow... Wherever you lift the veil of nature, you're bound to find a nice surprise.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Whether a place has four distinct seasons, is warm and pleasant all year round, has harsh extremes that flip from bitterly cold to scorching hot, or whatever else, it's just the result of natural evolution over thousands of years.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: ...And not a perfectly set up 'experimental environment.'

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: This place will never become 'Sami.'

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Sheesh. Do you know how much I wish I could grab you fellas and show you around Rhine HQ and Trimounts?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Sure, Sami is a mystery to me. But science is just as much a mystery to you guys.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Science can help us break the boundaries of nature. Shape new environments. It can help us... find answers.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: You're lying to yourself, Muelsyse.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hmm?
A tech company's exploration platform has discovered the last surviving grove of Pale Conifers in the mountainous region of northern Columbia...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: And what's that got to do with you?
There's a mountain village nearby, and though the population registry has been outdated for ages... some of the names in it match up with a missing persons list from Trenton.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Pretty sure not even Director Jara would be this concerned with what her employees get up to after hours.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Your behavior is far, far from gentlemanly, Justin Jr.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Hey now, don't get offended. I don't have any ulterior motives, and besides, I don't even know what you've been trying to track down.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: I just happened to catch a glance at this while negotiating a business deal, and figured a certain Director Muelsyse might agree to a date if she were interested.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Wait, is our well-connected Director of Business actually a coward? They don't keep me that busy over at Ecological, you know.

spans.text: Wait, is our well-connected Director of Business actually a coward? They don't keep me
busy over at Ecological, you know.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I'll come find you. Are you over at HQ?

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: At the café downstairs. I seem to recall you complaining about the decor in my office and refusing to enter.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I'll catch you at your office this time around then.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: You're back. Has it already been more than half a month since you left so suddenly?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: Icefield Cottongrass, she's...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I saw.
It is raining inside the vivarium.
Raindrops seep into the veins of the Zelkova leaves, drench the Square Sunflower's disc florets, and fall onto the stem of the withered plant next to them.
The rain is neither heavy nor fast, but seems to have no intention of stopping.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: Muelsyse, are you crying?

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: I don't blame you.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: That researcher, Kelly? She tried her best too...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Be it adding more nutrient solutions or replacing the substrate, they just can't compare to Sami's natural sustainability systems. But the Polar Area biome still isn't ready...

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: Hey, stop crying. You're drenching us in your tears and its killing me.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Maybe... Maybe I should delay the next batch of plants from Sami coming in next month.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: Hmm. Are you the type to be so easily shaken?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Well... exploring new scientific frontiers was never gonna be easy, and a setback or two was expected...

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: So why are you crying?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I made a trip to the mountains in northern Columbia, after my little chat with Justin Jr.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: Was it far?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Not really. Took me three or four days... I just ended up staying there for a whole week.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: If it wasn't far, why did you only make the trip now?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Because just finding the place took forever.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: From the orphanage in Trenton, to the deserted old houses, to the university in Trimounts, and to the laboratories of Rhine Lab...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: From the voluminous records in the library, to the nameless inscriptions, to experiment records with hardly any headway—yes, I even conducted experiments using samples taken from myself...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I spent a long, long time searching for it.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: And then finally I found it. Where I thought I'd find the answers about my parents, my people, and myself.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I have to turn this glass house into the cleanest place in Terra. It must have the freshest air, the most hospitable climate, and the most nutritious soil...

spans.text: to turn this glass house into the cleanest place in Terra. It
have the freshest air, the most hospitable climate, and the most nutritious soil...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It must have the richest ecosystem ever, for every kind of fragile life to freely thrive in.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: ...Including me.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: And that's why I need those answers. I have to know why my life is so frail, why I'm so sensitive to Originium Zones.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I need to know what I am, what 'Elves' are. I need to know how I was born, if my kin still reside on this land, and where... my future lies.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: ...And you came back without an answer.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: There was only a dilapidated mountain village, a patch of dying trees, and a simple and crude cemetery... Time has buried it all.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: There's no way to even tell if those Elves buried in the Pale Conifers had the answers I've been looking for, or if they were looking for them just as hopelessly as me.

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: Muelsyse, are you alright?

steps.name: Sheath Zelkova
steps.text: You look exhausted. Here, you can lean on my trunk.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You were right, Sunflower.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The vivarium's snowy mountains aren't actually mountains, and the icefield isn't an icefield. I'll never be able to recreate a 'Sami,' ever.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Because how can I, when I myself don't even know what kind of land I'm looking for?
The rainfall continues.
Rootless waterdrops form a pitter patter curtain of rain in the vivarium.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: Stop crying.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: It never rains like this in Sami. If you cry any more, you're going to destroy the Polar Area's ecology. And then the other plants will get sick, and you'll worry even more.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: You know...

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: The life cycle of Icefield Cottongrass really isn't long at all. When the winter wind on the icefield is at its strongest, not even a single cotton clump can hold onto its branches.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: Two days ago the Polar Area was practically smothered in white cotton wool. For a moment I really thought I was back on the Sami icefield.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: ...Thank you.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: It's Cottongrass's fault anyway, for being too curious. She was sending her clumps everywhere while you were away the past few days. They were all over the Polar Area, the Plateau Area, and the Ocean Area. She probably got her wish.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: She counted up all the plants in the entire vivarium... there's nearly a thousand species in here, and many of them should already be extinct from various ecological disasters.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: You said you wanted to build an ideal habitat here, but what you're actually doing is much more than that... Erm, when I put it that way, you're pretty similar to those other guys.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: I'm saying I've met people like you.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: Actually, I realized it from the start. I just wasn't completely sure... All of you can 'feel' us. You're all doing something similar, except you're doing it in a lab while they're in a forest.

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: Plants are their bandages, while the rain and dew serve as their painkillers... I think they were mending Sami's wounds.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Are you sure, Sunflower?

steps.name: Square Sunflower
steps.text: Of course, I even helped them out.
The rain stops.
Muelsyse stands in the center of the vivarium, pensively gazing at the plants in front of her.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I conducted two comparative experiments and the results were consistent. Basically, my deductions from dissecting and screening your samples were right.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: To date, the chemical composition of the seeds in your disc florets are unknown to academia, and they've proven to be decisive evidence for my conclusions.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You really are a super duper special plant. You have some kinda 'healing' property, we just don't know what exactly in nature you're meant to be healing.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But plants don't do that on their own.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: In other words, someone's putting you to use. And those someones are also a part of Sami's natural sustainability systems.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hey, Sami? Any of my people up there?
Sunlight penetrates the glass, and the Square Sunflower's drooping disc florets move ever so slightly.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Thank you, my imaginary friends.

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher
steps.text: Director Muelsyse...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher
steps.text: Uh, your... I'm so sorry for your loss!

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Umm...?

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher
steps.text: You can talk to plants, right? The Icefield Cottongrass... I...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Kelly! That's crazier than the rumors I hear about the old goat turning himself into a super cyborg to have late night boxing matches with Saria!

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher
steps.text: ...I-I apologize.

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher
steps.text: Ah, right. I came to hand you this letter.

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher
steps.text: They're invitations from the leading scientific journals. You know, 'The TIT Academic Journal', 'Biology Review', and 'Nature Communications.' They're all really interested in your recent research results.

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher
steps.text: Your plant information experiments have proven workable in the fields of both plant physiology and plant phylogenetics. This marks a major breakthrough in ecology.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hey now, I don't deserve all the credit. You guys helped too!

spans.text: the credit. You guys helped too!

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher
steps.text: So what should we do with the invitations?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: We'll take their offers, but could you write back to the editors for me? The submissions might come a teensy bit late.

steps.name: Ecological Section Researcher
steps.text: Are you taking some time off? You did just throw yourself back into your work right after that long trip.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Nope. I'm taking a little trip to Sami.
